verses.text: Now dis na di names of Israel pikin man dem wey come into Egypt with Jacob, every man with im household:
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
All di souls wey come out of Jacob body na 70 souls, and Joseph dey Egypt already.
Joseph die, and all im brothers, and all dat generation.
Di pikin dem of Israel born plenty pikin, increase abundantly, multiply, and become very mighty. Di land fill with dem.
Now one new king rise up over Egypt, wey no know Joseph.
E talk to im people, “Look, di people of di pikin dem of Israel plenty and mightier pass us.
Come, make we deal wisely with dem, or else dem go multiply, and e go happen say if war break out, dem go join demself to our enemies, fight against us, and leave di land.”
So dem set taskmasters over dem to afflict dem with hard labour. Dem build store cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses.
But di more dem afflict dem, di more dem multiply and spread out. Dem dey grieved because of di pikin dem of Israel.
Di Egyptians make di pikin dem of Israel serve with rigor,
and dem make dem life bitter with hard service, for mortar and for brick, and for all kinds of service for di field, all dem service wey dem make dem serve with rigor.
Di king of Egypt talk to di Hebrew midwives, wey di name of one na Shiphrah, and di name of di other na Puah:
e talk, “When una do di work of midwife for di Hebrew women, and see dem for di birth stool, if na pikin man, una go kill am; but if na pikin woman, e go live.”
But di midwives fear God, and no do as di king of Egypt command dem, but dem save di pikin man dem alive.
Di king of Egypt call di midwives, and talk to dem, “Why una don do dis thing, and don save di pikin man dem alive?”
Di midwives talk to Pharaoh, “Because di Hebrew women no be like di Egyptian women, because dem dey lively, and don born before di midwife come to dem.”
God deal well with di midwives. Di people multiply, and become very mighty.
E come be say, because di midwives fear God, e give dem households.
Pharaoh command all im people, say, “Every pikin man wey dem born, una go throw am into di river, and every pikin woman una go save alive.”
One man of di house of Levi go marry one pikin woman of Levi.
Di woman become pregnant, and born one pikin man. When e see am say e fine, e hide am three months.
When e no fit hide am again, e take for am one papyrus basket, daub am with tar and with pitch, put di pikin inside, and lay am among di reeds by di riverbank.
Im sister stand far away to know wetin go happen to am.
Pharaoh pikin woman come down to bathe at di river. Im maidens dey waka along di riverside. E see di basket among di reeds, and send im servant to fetch am.
E open am, and see di pikin, and look, di boy dey cry. E feel compassion for am, and talk, “Dis na one of di Hebrews pikin dem.”
Den im sister talk to Pharaoh pikin woman, “I go go call one nurse for you from di Hebrew women, so that e go nurse di pikin for you?”
Pharaoh pikin woman talk to am, “Go.” Di girl go call di pikin mama.
Pharaoh pikin woman talk to am, “Take dis pikin away, and nurse am for me, and I go pay your wages.” Di woman take di pikin, and nurse am.
Di pikin grow, and e bring am to Pharaoh pikin woman, and e become im pikin. E call im name Moses, and talk, “Because I draw am out of di water.”
E come be say for dem days, when Moses don grow up, e go out to im brothers, and look at dem burdens. E see one Egyptian dey strike one Hebrew, one of im brothers.
E look dis way and dat way, and when e see say nobody dey, e kill di Egyptian, and hide am for di sand.
E go out di second day, and look, two men of di Hebrews dey fight with each other. E talk to di one wey dey wrong, “Why you dey strike your fellow?”
E talk, “Who make you ruler and judge over us? You dey think to kill me, as you kill di Egyptian?” Moses fear, and talk, “Surely di thing don dey known.”
When Pharaoh hear dis thing, e try to kill Moses. But Moses flee from di face of Pharaoh, and dwell for di land of Midian, and sit down by one well.
Now di priest of Midian get seven pikin woman dem. Dem come draw water, and fill di troughs to water dem papa flock.
Di shepherds come and drive dem away, but Moses stand up and help dem, and water dem flock.
When dem come to Reuel dem papa, e talk, “Why una don come so soon today?”
Dem talk, “One Egyptian rescue us from di hand of di shepherds, and e even draw water for us, and water di flock.”
E talk to im pikin woman dem, “Wia e dey? Why una don leave di man? Call am, make e eat bread.”
Moses agree to dwell with di man. E give Moses im pikin woman Zipporah.
Zipporah born one pikin man, and Moses call im name Gershom, because e talk, “I don dey stranger for strange land.”
E come be say for dem many days, di king of Egypt die, and di pikin dem of Israel groan because of di bondage, and dem cry, and dem cry for help come up to God because of di bondage.
God hear dem groaning, and God remember im covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
God see di pikin dem of Israel, and God take notice.
Now Moses dey keep di flock of Jethro, im wife papa, di priest of Midian. E lead di flock to di back of di wilderness, and come to God mountain, to Horeb.
Di angel of di Lord appear to am for flame of fire out of di middle of one bush. E look, and look, di bush dey burn with fire, but di bush no dey consumed.
Moses talk, “I go turn aside now, and see dis great sight, why di bush no dey burn up.”
When di Lord see say e turn aside to see, God call to am out of di middle of di bush, and talk, “Moses, Moses!” E talk, “Here I dey.”
E talk, “No come near here. Take your sandals off your feet, because di place wia you dey stand na holy ground.”
Moreover e talk, “I na di God of your papa, di God of Abraham, di God of Isaac, and di God of Jacob.” Moses hide im face, because e dey afraid to look at God.
Di Lord talk, “I don surely see di affliction of my people wey dey for Egypt, and I don hear dem cry because of dem taskmasters, because I know dem sorrows.

I don come down to deliver dem out of di hand of di Egyptians, and to bring dem up out of dat land to one good and large land, to one land wey dey flow with milk and honey, to di place of di Canaanites, di Hittites, di Amorites, di Perizzites, di Hivites, and di Jebusites.
Now look, di cry of di pikin dem of Israel don come to me. Moreover I don see di oppression wey di Egyptians oppress dem.
Come now therefore, and I go send you to Pharaoh, so that you go bring my people, di pikin dem of Israel, out of Egypt.”
Moses talk to God, “Who be me, say I go go to Pharaoh, and say I go bring di pikin dem of Israel out of Egypt?”
E talk, “Certainly I go dey with you. Dis go be di token to you, say I don send you: when you don bring di people out of Egypt, una go serve God for dis mountain.”
Moses talk to God, “Look, when I come to di pikin dem of Israel, and talk to dem, ‘Di God of una papa dem don send me to una,’ and dem talk to me, ‘Wetin im name be?’ wetin I go talk to dem?”
God talk to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and e talk, “Dis na wetin you go talk to di pikin dem of Israel: ‘I AM don send me to una.’”

God talk moreover to Moses, “Dis na wetin you go talk to di pikin dem of Israel: ‘Di Lord, di God of una papa dem, di God of Abraham, di God of Isaac, and di God of Jacob, don send me to una.’ Dis na my name forever, and dis na my memorial to all generations.

Go, and gather di elders of Israel together, and talk to dem, ‘Di Lord, di God of una papa dem, di God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, appear to me, talk so: I don surely visit una, and see wetin dem do to una for Egypt.

I don talk say I go bring una up out of di affliction of Egypt to di land of di Canaanites, di Hittites, di Amorites, di Perizzites, di Hivites, and di Jebusites, to one land wey dey flow with milk and honey.’

Dem go listen to your voice. Una go come, you and di elders of Israel, to di king of Egypt, and una go talk to am, ‘Di Lord, di God of di Hebrews, don meet with us. Now make we go three days journey into di wilderness, so that we go sacrifice to di Lord our God.’
I know say di king of Egypt no go let una go, no, not by mighty hand.
I go stretch out my hand, and strike Egypt with all my wonders wey I go do inside am. After dat e go let una go.
I go give dis people favour for di sight of di Egyptians. E go come be say, when una go, una no go go empty.

But every woman go ask im neighbour, and di one wey dey stay for im house, jewels of silver, jewels of gold, and clothing. Una go put dem on una pikin man dem, and on una pikin woman dem. Una go plunder di Egyptians.”
Moses answer, “But look, dem no go believe me, nor listen to my voice, because dem go talk, ‘Di Lord no appear to you.’”
Di Lord talk to am, “Wetin dey your hand?” E talk, “One rod.”
E talk, “Throw am on di ground.” E throw am on di ground, and e become serpent, and Moses run from am.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Put out your hand, and take am by di tail.” E put out im hand, and hold am, and e become rod for im hand.
“So that dem go believe say di Lord, di God of dem papa dem, di God of Abraham, di God of Isaac, and di God of Jacob, don appear to you.”
Di Lord talk moreover to am, “Put your hand inside your cloak.” E put im hand inside im cloak, and when e take am out, look, im hand dey leprous, as white as snow.
E talk, “Put your hand inside your cloak again.” E put im hand inside im cloak again, and when e take am out of im cloak, look, e don turn again as im other flesh.
“E go happen, if dem no believe you, nor listen to di voice of di first sign, say dem go believe di voice of di latter sign.

E go happen, if dem no believe even dem two signs, nor listen to your voice, say you go take of di water of di river, and pour am on di dry land. Di water wey you take out of di river go become blood on di dry land.”
Moses talk to di Lord, “Oh Lord, I no be eloquent, neither before nor since you don talk to your servant, but I dey slow of speech, and slow of tongue.”
Di Lord talk to am, “Who don make man mouth? Or who make di mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? No be me, di Lord?
Now therefore go, and I go dey with your mouth, and teach you wetin you go talk.”
E talk, “Oh Lord, make you send di one wey you go send.”
Di Lord anger burn against Moses, and e talk, “Aaron di Levite no be your brother? I know say e fit speak well. Look, e even dey come out to meet you. When e see you, e go glad for im heart.
You go speak to am, and put di words for im mouth. I go dey with your mouth, and with im mouth, and I go teach una wetin una go do.
E go be your spokesman to di people. E go be, even e go be to you for mouth, and you go be to am as God.
You go take dis rod for your hand, with wey you go do di signs.”
Moses go and return to im wife papa Jethro, and talk to am, “Make I go, and return to my brothers wey dey Egypt, and see whether dem still dey alive.” Jethro talk to Moses, “Go in peace.”
Di Lord talk to Moses for Midian, “Go, return into Egypt, because all di men wey seek your life don die.”
Moses take im wife and im pikin man dem, and set dem on one donkey, and e return to di land of Egypt. Moses take di rod of God for im hand.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “When you go back into Egypt, see say you do before Pharaoh all di wonders wey I don put for your hand, but I go harden im heart, so that e no go let di people go.
Una go talk to Pharaoh, ‘Di Lord talk so: Israel na my pikin, my firstborn,
and I don talk to you, make you let my pikin go, so that e go serve me, and you don refuse to let am go. Look, I go kill your pikin, your firstborn.’”
E come be say for di way, for di inn, di Lord meet am, and seek to kill am.
Den Zipporah take one flint, cut off di foreskin of im pikin man, cast am at im feet, and talk, “Surely you na bridegroom of blood to me.”
So e let am go. Den e talk, “Bridegroom of blood,” because of di circumcision.
Di Lord talk to Aaron, “Go into di wilderness to meet Moses.” E go, and meet am for God mountain, and kiss am.
Moses tell Aaron all di words of di Lord wey e send am, and all di signs wey e command am.
Moses and Aaron go and gather together all di elders of di pikin dem of Israel.
Aaron speak all di words wey di Lord don talk to Moses, and do di signs for di sight of di people.
Di people believe. When dem hear say di Lord don visit di pikin dem of Israel, and say e don see dem affliction, dem bow dem heads and worship.
Afterward Moses and Aaron come, and talk to Pharaoh, “Di Lord, di God of Israel, talk so: ‘Make you let my people go, so that dem go hold feast to me for di wilderness.’”
Pharaoh talk, “Who be di Lord, say I go obey im voice to let Israel go? I no know di Lord, and moreover I no go let Israel go.”
Dem talk, “Di God of di Hebrews don meet with us. Make we go three days journey into di wilderness, and sacrifice to di Lord our God, otherwise e go fall on us with pestilence or with sword.”
Di king of Egypt talk to dem, “Moses and Aaron, why una dey take di people from dem work? Go to una burdens.”
Pharaoh talk, “Look, di people of di land dey plenty now, and una make dem rest from dem burdens.”
Di same day Pharaoh command di taskmasters of di people, and dem officers, talk,
“Una no go give di people straw to make bricks again, as before. Make dem go and gather straw for demself.
Di number of di bricks wey dem make before, una go lay on dem. Una no go reduce am, because dem dey idle. Na why dem cry, talk, ‘Make we go and sacrifice to our God.’
Make more work dey laid on di men, make dem labour for am, and make dem no regard lying words.”
Di taskmasters of di people go out, and dem officers, and dem speak to di people, talk, “Pharaoh talk so: ‘I no go give una straw.
Una go yourselves, get straw where una fit find am, but nothing of una work go dey reduced.’”
So di people scatter abroad throughout all di land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
Di taskmasters press dem, talk, “Fulfill your work, your daily tasks, as when di straw dey.”
Di officers of di pikin dem of Israel, wey Pharaoh taskmasters set over dem, dem beat dem, and dem demand, “Why una no fulfill una task of making brick yesterday and today, as before?”
Den di officers of di pikin dem of Israel come and cry to Pharaoh, talk, “Why you deal so with your servants?
Dem no give your servants straw, and dem talk to us, ‘Make bricks!’ Look, your servants dey beaten, but di fault na for your own people.”
But e talk, “Una dey idle! Una dey idle! Na why una talk, ‘Make we go and sacrifice to di Lord.’
Go therefore now, and work, because dem no go give una straw, yet una go deliver di same number of bricks.”
Di officers of di pikin dem of Israel see say dem dey for trouble, when dem hear say una no go reduce anything from una bricks, from una daily tasks.
Dem meet Moses and Aaron, wey stand for di way as dem come out from Pharaoh.
Dem talk to dem, “Make di Lord look on una, and judge, because una don make us stink before Pharaoh, and before im servants, to put one sword for dem hand to kill us.”
Moses return to di Lord, and talk, “Lord, why you don mistreat dis people? Why you don send me?
Because since I come to Pharaoh to speak for your name, e don mistreat dis people. You no deliver your people at all.”
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Now you go see wetin I go do to Pharaoh. By strong hand e go let dem go, and by strong hand e go drive dem out of im land.”
God talk to Moses, and talk to am, “I na di Lord.
I appear to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God, but by my name di Lord I no make myself known to dem.
I establish my covenant with dem too, to give dem di land of Canaan, di land wia dem dey sojourn, wia dem dey stranger.
Moreover I don hear di groaning of di pikin dem of Israel, wey di Egyptians dey keep for bondage, and I don remember my covenant.

Na why say to di pikin dem of Israel, ‘I na di Lord, and I go bring una out from under di burdens of di Egyptians, and I go rescue una from dem bondage. I go redeem una with outstretched arm, and with great judgments.
I go take una for my people, and I go be una God. Una go know say I na di Lord una God, wey bring una out from under di burdens of di Egyptians.
I go bring una into di land wey I swear to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and I go give am to una for possession. I na di Lord.’”
Moses speak so to di pikin dem of Israel, but dem no listen to Moses because of anguish of spirit and hard bondage.
Di Lord speak to Moses, talk,
“Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, make e let di pikin dem of Israel go out of im land.”
Moses speak before di Lord, talk, “Look, di pikin dem of Israel no listen to me. How den Pharaoh go listen to me, wey be of uncircumcised lips?”
Di Lord speak to Moses and to Aaron, and give dem command to di pikin dem of Israel, and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring di pikin dem of Israel out of di land of Egypt.
Dem na di heads of dem papa houses. Di pikin dem of Reuben, di firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. Dem na di families of Reuben.
Di pikin dem of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, di pikin of one Canaanite woman. Dem na di families of Simeon.
Dem na di names of di pikin dem of Levi according to dem generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Di years of di life of Levi na 137 years.
Di pikin dem of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to dem families.
Di pikin dem of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Di years of di life of Kohath na 133 years.
Di pikin dem of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. Dem na di families of di Levites according to dem generations.
Amram take Jochebed im papa sister to be im wife, and e born am Aaron and Moses. Di years of di life of Amram na 137 years.
Di pikin dem of Izhar: Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
Di pikin dem of Uzziel: Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
Aaron take Elisheba, di pikin woman of Amminadab, di sister of Nahshon, to be im wife, and e born am Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Di pikin dem of Korah: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. Dem na di families of di Korahites.
Eleazar, Aaron pikin, take one of di pikin woman dem of Putiel to be im wife, and e born am Phinehas. Dem na di heads of di papa houses of di Levites according to dem families.
Dem na Aaron and Moses, wey di Lord talk to say, “Bring out di pikin dem of Israel from di land of Egypt according to dem armies.”
Dem na di ones wey speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out di pikin dem of Israel from Egypt. Dem na Moses and Aaron.
E come be say for di day wey di Lord speak to Moses for di land of Egypt,
di Lord speak to Moses, talk, “I na di Lord. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all wey I speak to you.”
Moses talk before di Lord, “Look, I be of uncircumcised lips, and how Pharaoh go listen to me?”
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Look, I don make you as God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother go be your prophet.
You go speak all wey I command you, and Aaron your brother go speak to Pharaoh, make e let di pikin dem of Israel go out of im land.
I go harden Pharaoh heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders for di land of Egypt.
But Pharaoh no go listen to una, and I go lay my hand on Egypt, and bring out my armies, my people di pikin dem of Israel, out of di land of Egypt by great judgments.
Di Egyptians go know say I na di Lord, when I stretch out my hand on Egypt, and bring out di pikin dem of Israel from among dem.”
Moses and Aaron do so. As di Lord command dem, so dem do.
Moses dey 80 years old, and Aaron 83 years old, when dem speak to Pharaoh.
Di Lord speak to Moses and Aaron, talk,
“When Pharaoh go speak to una, talk, ‘Show one miracle for yourselves,’ you go talk to Aaron, ‘Take your rod, and cast am down before Pharaoh,’ and e go become serpent.”
Moses and Aaron go in to Pharaoh, and dem do so, as di Lord command. Aaron cast down im rod before Pharaoh and before im servants, and e become serpent.
Den Pharaoh too call di wise men and di sorcerers. Di magicians of Egypt, dem too, do di same thing with dem enchantments.
Dem cast down every man im rod, and dem become serpents, but Aaron rod swallow up dem rods.
Pharaoh heart harden, and e no listen to dem, as di Lord don talk.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Pharaoh heart dey stubborn. E refuse to let di people go.
Go to Pharaoh for morning. Look, e dey go out to di water. You go stand by di riverbank to meet am. Di rod wey turn to serpent, you go take am for your hand.
You go talk to am, ‘Di Lord, di God of di Hebrews, don send me to you, wey talk so: Make you let my people go, so that dem go serve me for di wilderness. Look, till now you no listen.
Di Lord talk so: By dis you go know say I na di Lord. Look, I go strike with di rod wey dey my hand di waters wey dey di river, and dem go turn to blood.
Di fish wey dey di river go die, and di river go stink. Di Egyptians go loathe to drink water from di river.’”

Di Lord talk to Moses, “Talk to Aaron, ‘Take your rod, and stretch out your hand over di waters of Egypt, over dem rivers, over dem streams, over dem pools, and over all dem ponds of water, so that dem go become blood. Blood go dey throughout all di land of Egypt, both for vessels of wood and for vessels of stone.’”

Moses and Aaron do so, as di Lord command. E lift up di rod, and strike di waters wey dey di river, for di sight of Pharaoh, and for di sight of im servants, and all di waters wey dey di river turn to blood.
Di fish wey dey di river die. Di river stink, and di Egyptians no fit drink water from di river. Di blood dey throughout all di land of Egypt.
Di magicians of Egypt do di same thing with dem enchantments. Pharaoh heart harden, and e no listen to dem, as di Lord don talk.
Pharaoh turn and go into im house, and e no set im heart to dis too.
All di Egyptians dig round di river for water to drink, because dem no fit drink of di water of di river.
Seven days complete, after di Lord don strike di river.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, and talk to am, ‘Di Lord talk so: Make you let my people go, so that dem go serve me.
If you refuse to let dem go, look, I go plague all your borders with frogs.

Di river go swarm with frogs, wey go go up and come into your house, and into your bedroom, and on your bed, and into di house of your servants, and on your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading troughs.
Di frogs go come up both on you, and on your people, and on all your servants.’”
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Talk to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your rod over di rivers, over di streams, and over di pools, and cause frogs to come up on di land of Egypt.’”
Aaron stretch out im hand over di waters of Egypt, and di frogs come up, and cover di land of Egypt.
Di magicians do di same thing with dem enchantments, and bring up frogs on di land of Egypt.
Den Pharaoh call for Moses and Aaron, and talk, “Pray to di Lord, make e take away di frogs from me and from my people, and I go let di people go, so that dem go sacrifice to di Lord.”

Moses talk to Pharaoh, “Glorify yourself over me: when I go pray for you, and for your servants, and for your people, so that di frogs go dey destroyed from you and your houses, and remain for di river only?”
E talk, “Tomorrow.” E talk, “Make am be according to your word, so that you go know say nobody dey like di Lord our God.
Di frogs go depart from you, and from your houses, and from your servants, and from your people. Dem go remain for di river only.”
Moses and Aaron go out from Pharaoh, and Moses cry to di Lord concerning di frogs wey e bring on Pharaoh.
Di Lord do according to di word of Moses, and di frogs die out of di houses, out of di courts, and out of di fields.
Dem gather dem together in heaps, and di land stink.
But when Pharaoh see say e get relief, e harden im heart, and no listen to dem, as di Lord don talk.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Talk to Aaron, ‘Stretch out your rod, and strike di dust of di earth, so that e go become lice throughout all di land of Egypt.’”
Dem do so. Aaron stretch out im hand with im rod, and strike di dust of di earth, and e become lice on man and on animal. All di dust of di earth become lice throughout all di land of Egypt.
Di magicians try with dem enchantments to bring forth lice, but dem no fit. Di lice dey on man and on animal.
Den di magicians talk to Pharaoh, “Dis na di finger of God.” Pharaoh heart harden, and e no listen to dem, as di Lord don talk.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Rise up early for morning, and stand before Pharaoh. Look, e dey come out to di water. Talk to am, ‘Di Lord talk so: Make you let my people go, so that dem go serve me.

Or else, if you no let my people go, look, I go send swarms of flies on you, and on your servants, and on your people, and into your houses. Di houses of di Egyptians go dey full of swarms of flies, and di ground too wia dem dey.
I go set apart for dat day di land of Goshen, wia my people dey dwell, so that no swarms of flies go dey dere, so that you go know say I na di Lord for di middle of di earth.
I go put division between my people and your people. Tomorrow dis sign go be.’”
Di Lord do so. Thick swarms of flies come into Pharaoh house, and into im servants houses, and into all di land of Egypt. Di land dey ruined because of di swarms of flies.
Pharaoh call for Moses and for Aaron, and talk, “Go, sacrifice to your God for di land.”
Moses talk, “E no right to do so, because we go sacrifice di abomination of di Egyptians to di Lord our God. Look, if we sacrifice di abomination of di Egyptians before dem eyes, dem no go stone us?
We go go three days journey into di wilderness, and sacrifice to di Lord our God, as e go command us.”
Pharaoh talk, “I go let una go, so that una go sacrifice to di Lord una God for di wilderness, only una no go go very far away. Pray for me.”

Moses talk, “Look, I dey go out from you, and I go pray to di Lord make di swarms of flies depart from Pharaoh, from im servants, and from im people tomorrow, only make Pharaoh no deal deceitfully again by not letting di people go to sacrifice to di Lord.”
Moses go out from Pharaoh, and pray to di Lord.
Di Lord do according to di word of Moses, and e remove di swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from im servants, and from im people. Not one remain.
Pharaoh harden im heart dis time too, and e no let di people go.
Den di Lord talk to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, and talk to am, ‘Di Lord, di God of di Hebrews, talk so: Make you let my people go, so that dem go serve me.
Because if you refuse to let dem go, and hold dem still,
look, di hand of di Lord dey on your livestock wey dey di field, on di horses, on di donkeys, on di camels, on di herds, and on di flocks, with very grievous pestilence.
Di Lord go make distinction between di livestock of Israel and di livestock of Egypt, so that nothing go die of all wey belong to di pikin dem of Israel.’”
Di Lord appoint set time, talk, “Tomorrow di Lord go do dis thing for di land.”
Di Lord do dat thing on di next day, and all di livestock of Egypt die, but of di livestock of di pikin dem of Israel, not one die.
Pharaoh send, and look, not even one of di livestock of di Israelites dey dead. But di heart of Pharaoh harden, and e no let di people go.
Di Lord talk to Moses and to Aaron, “Take to yourselves handfuls of ashes of di furnace, and make Moses sprinkle am toward di sky for di sight of Pharaoh.
E go become small dust over all di land of Egypt, and go become boils breaking out with sores on man and on animal throughout all di land of Egypt.”
Dem take ashes of di furnace, and stand before Pharaoh. Moses sprinkle am up toward di sky, and e become boils breaking out with sores on man and on animal.
Di magicians no fit stand before Moses because of di boils, because di boils dey on di magicians, and on all di Egyptians.
Di Lord harden di heart of Pharaoh, and e no listen to dem, as di Lord don talk to Moses.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Rise up early for morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and talk to am, ‘Di Lord, di God of di Hebrews, talk so: Make you let my people go, so that dem go serve me.
Because dis time I go send all my plagues on your heart, and on your servants, and on your people, so that you go know say nobody dey like me for all di earth.
Because now I for don stretch out my hand, and strike you and your people with pestilence, and you for don dey cut off from di earth.
But in very deed for dis cause I don make you stand, to show you my power, and so that my name go dey declared throughout all di earth.
You still exalt yourself against my people, say you no go let dem go.
Look, tomorrow about dis time I go cause very grievous hail to rain down, such as no dey for Egypt since di day wey e found even until now.
Send now therefore, and gather your livestock and all wey you get for di field. Di hail go come down on every man and animal wey dey found for di field, and no dey brought home, and dem go die.’”
Di one among di servants of Pharaoh wey fear di word of di Lord make im servants and im livestock flee into di houses,
but im wey no regard di word of di Lord leave im servants and im livestock for di field.
Di Lord talk to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward di sky, so that hail go dey for all di land of Egypt, on man, on animal, and on every herb of di field, throughout di land of Egypt.”
Moses stretch out im rod toward di sky, and di Lord send thunder and hail, and fire run down to di earth. Di Lord rain hail on di land of Egypt.
So dere dey hail, and fire flashing continually inside di hail, very grievous, such as no dey for all di land of Egypt since e become nation.
Di hail strike throughout all di land of Egypt all wey dey di field, both man and animal. Di hail strike every herb of di field, and break every tree of di field.
Only for di land of Goshen, wia di pikin dem of Israel dey, hail no dey.
Pharaoh send, and call for Moses and Aaron, and talk to dem, “I don sin dis time. Di Lord na righteous, and I and my people na wicked.
Pray to di Lord, because e don enough. Make dere no be mighty thunderings and hail again. I go let una go, and una no go stay any longer.”
Moses talk to am, “As soon as I don go out of di city, I go spread out my hands to di Lord. Di thunders go cease, and dere no go dey hail anymore, so that you go know say di earth belong to di Lord.
But as for you and your servants, I know say you no go yet fear di Lord God.”
Di flax and di barley dey struck, because di barley dey ear, and di flax dey bloom.
But di wheat and di spelt no dey struck, because dem no dey grown up.
Moses go out of di city from Pharaoh, and spread out im hands to di Lord. Di thunders and hail cease, and rain no pour on di earth again.
When Pharaoh see say di rain and di hail and di thunders cease, e sin yet more, and harden im heart, e and im servants.
Di heart of Pharaoh harden, and e no let di pikin dem of Israel go, as di Lord don talk by Moses.
